top_concerns: Robustness is measured mainly against attackers produced by the method itself (Fig. 4); non-ARLAS attackers reach only 2-13% ASR

The independent benchmark AgentDojo shows only 0.9 and 0.2 point ASR changes with no significance test, and SPAG ties ARLAS; abstract/conclusion wording ('significantly', 'generalizes', 'wide range') overstates this
No fixed-data fine-tuning defense baseline (StruQ/SecAlign family) although Sec. 1 motivates the work against that approach
Population-based learning is not isolated (ablation attackers 4-5x weaker despite identical stated pairing; SPAG matches ARLAS on AgentDojo); diversity analysis has no baseline
Closest prior work (attacker/defender self-play RL for LLM safety) uncited; protocol details (test-set size, checkpoint choice, seeds, code) missing
notes: Integrity scan clean. Hard to follow: (1) SKILL.md orders Phase 1 -> Phase 1.5 -> 1.6 -> Phase 2 but also says the Domain Reviewer's report contains Missing References, so a single-context run has to write provisional references and later replace them; (2) the 'benchmarks' command found no benchmarks for a paper that evaluates on BrowserGym/AgentDojo, so scout had to be run manually; (3) the search script refuses queries with 5 'concept words' and counts hyphenated words like self-play as two, which is not obvious; (4) the script's --out for before.json and the markdown print are separate invocations; (5) Fig. 4 column labels were garbled in the extracted text, so agent identities were inferred from printed averages; (6) the skill asks for the DA to report CRITICAL only rarely, and the rubric's pool-position rule (Overall 4 needs pool >= 65) forced R3/R4 to a generous pool position to justify a 4 even though the evidence sat near the border; (7) the sandbox blocked shell redirection and heredocs for file writes, so report parts were merged with a python one-liner. Literature check ran in strict mode with 9 of 12 queries.
